headline: Singer Asif Akbar's car targeted with gunfire in Mogbazar, Dhaka; he was not present
summary: Unidentified assailants shot at the personal vehicle of popular singer and former BCB director Asif Akbar early Saturday morning in Mogbazar. Fortunately, Akbar was not inside the car at the time of the incident and remains unharmed.
details: Unidentified assailants fired shots at the personal car of popular singer and former BCB director Asif Akbar. The incident occurred early Saturday morning around 5 AM in Dhaka's Mogbazar area.
Police confirmed that Asif Akbar was not present in the vehicle when the shots were fired. Consequently, he remained unharmed during the attack.

The identities of the perpetrators and the motive behind the attack are currently unknown. Authorities have not yet confirmed any links between the incident and Akbar's personal or professional disputes.
Asif Akbar is a well-known figure in both the music and cricket industries. He has previously served as a director of the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB).

headline: Shops return to 8 PM closing as Durga Puja holiday hours end
summary: Shopping malls, markets, and stores in Bangladesh have reverted to their original operating hours, closing at 8 PM. This change follows the end of a temporary extension granted for the Durga Puja festival.
details: Shopping malls, markets, and stores across Bangladesh have returned to their previous operating schedules, with closing times now set at 8 PM. This adjustment comes as the temporary extension granted for the Sharadiya Durga Puja festival has concluded.

Previously, on October 5, the Ministry of Power had permitted shopping malls, markets, and stores to remain open until 10 PM, with this allowance valid until October 22. This special provision was made in observance of the Durga Puja celebrations.
As per the ministry's directive, the earlier stipulated timings would be reinstated from October 23. Consequently, these establishments are now permitted to operate only between 11 AM and 8 PM.

This move is part of a broader initiative by the government to conserve electricity and manage energy resources more effectively. An order issued on August 12 had mandated that all shopping malls, stores, and markets nationwide must close by 8 PM.
Furthermore, the directive from the power division also included a stipulation against decorative lighting in shops and shopping malls after 7 PM, aiming to further reduce electricity consumption.
